ui_reference.title: 22. Interface Reference (10 screens)
ui_reference.content:
22. Interface reference

One entry per screen, with a capture of that screen taken from the running program. A validation case is loaded in every capture, so the panels show real content. The captures are generated when the documentation is built, never pasted by hand: a pasted screenshot goes stale silently when the interface changes.

The module bar at the top of the window switches between Model, Contacts, Loads, Analysis, Results and Report. Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+6 do the same, Ctrl+R runs, and Shift+F frames the drawing.

22.1 Model

The joint as the solver sees it: a chain of mass-spring-damper elements between the bolt head and the nut, with the clamped members in parallel and each contact in series. This canvas is the MSD Builder, hosted inside the module rather than opened as a separate window, so what you draw here is what runs.

Capture of Model at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Palette on the left: drag an element type onto the grid to add it to the chain.
  • Double-click an element to edit it; the Element tab of the inspector opens on the right.
  • The schematic and the model are kept in sync in both directions: an edit here updates the model, and loading a case rebuilds the drawing.
  • Shift+F frames the contents; the framing re-arms whenever a new model is loaded, so an imported case is never left as a speck in a corner.

22.2 Contacts

The same chain, with the tribological interfaces in focus. Two of them decide loosening: the bearing face under the head or nut, and the thread flank. Friction and wear live on these, not on the bolt.

Capture of Contacts at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Select an interface to open the Contact tab of the inspector.
  • Friction is set at two levels: a persistent value on the model and an in-session value on the loading, and the solver honours the more specific one.
  • A case loaded from the validation corpus arrives with the friction coefficient of its adopted configuration already in place.

22.3 Loads

Where the excitation is defined and where you can see how it flows through the joint. Transverse displacement-controlled loading is the Junker condition; axial force-controlled loading is the other family in the corpus.

Capture of Loads at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Loading type, amplitude, frequency and cycle count.
  • Preload, in newtons or as a percentage of yield; leaving the force at zero makes the model compute it from the percentage.
  • The load-flow overlay annotates the chain with the share each element carries, which is the quickest way to see an implausible stiffness partition before running anything.

22.4 Analysis

Solver settings and the run itself. The integration is cycle by cycle over a slow state, so the settings that matter are the ones that decide how many cycles are integrated and how finely.

Capture of Analysis at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Cycle count and the sub-stepping inside a cycle.
  • Which loss mechanisms are active: embedding, creep, fretting wear and nut rotation act in parallel and can be examined one at a time.
  • Ctrl+R runs from any module.

22.5 Results

Two sub-tabs: Run shows the curves of the analysis you just ran, and Validation is the corpus browser. Section 20 of this documentation lists the sources behind it.

Capture of Results at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Run: preload against cycles, the mechanism decomposition, the friction and phase plots.
  • Validation: the tree of sources and curves, described in the next entry.
  • The context bar above the viewport switches between plot families without leaving the module.

22.6 Results → Validation

The corpus, as a tree of source paper → curve. Every curve carries the model's mean absolute error against the digitised measurement, so the quality of the fit is visible before you open anything.

Capture of Results → Validation at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Abrir no Model/Run loads that curve as the editable model, with the adopted constants of its case, and switches to the Model module.
  • Re-simular caso and Re-simular tudo run the engine again and rewrite the stored result.
  • Report HTML opens the full report of that case: conditions, the mass-spring-damper model, the residual against the three legs of the acceptance criterion, the mechanism decomposition and every constant with its provenance.
  • Salvar caso como .msd writes the model to a file with the adopted configuration and the citation of the source paper inside it. The whole corpus is already saved that way under Models/SAVED_CASES/.
  • The highlighted intake panel at the top imports a case of your own from a .bascase.json file.

22.7 Report

Assembles a document from the current analysis. The per-case reports of the validation corpus are generated from the same machinery, which is why a report of your own joint has the same sections as the ones behind Section 20.

Capture of Report at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Choice of sections to include.
  • Export to HTML; the report opens in the system browser rather than in an embedded view, so no web engine is required.

22.8 Inspector → Element

The properties of the selected element. Stiffness, damping and mass can be typed directly or computed from geometry and material, which is the usual choice: a bolt's stiffness follows from its diameter, grip length and modulus.

Capture of Inspector → Element at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • k, c and m, each with an auto-calculate switch. With the switch on, the value is recomputed from geometry and material whenever either changes.
  • Geometry: diameter, length, thread pitch.
  • Material, from the bundled database.
  • A case from the corpus arrives with the geometry overrides of its adopted configuration already applied.

22.9 Inspector → Loading

The excitation and the preload of the selected loading, at the level that applies in the current session.

Capture of Inspector → Loading at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Preload force, or percentage of yield.
  • Transverse displacement amplitude, or axial force amplitude.
  • Frequency and number of cycles.
  • The in-session friction coefficient, which overrides the persistent one on the model.

22.10 Inspector → Contact

The tribology of the selected interface: this is where the constants that the validation calibrates actually live.

Capture of Inspector → Contact at 1500×900 px, with case lu2024_M8_fig18_amp0p5 loaded.

Controls

  • Friction coefficient of the interface.
  • Contact stiffness and the embedding parameters.
  • Wear coefficients.
  • For a case from the corpus, these are the adopted constants; the provenance of each one is in the case report (Section 20).
